title: Time compactness: which hypotheses can be transferred?
audience: Early doctoral PDE analysts who can calculate Bochner integrals, use Holder and Minkowski, and recognize strong subsequence convergence, but have not learned nonlinear Aubin--Lions arguments.
reader_goals: Test the compactness conclusion against the infinity endpoint and the nonlinear-image unknown.
Distinguish the r>1 truncation estimate from a claimed necessary condition.
Audit inverse-lift measurability, injectivity and derivative/output-space matching before transferring a theorem.
prerequisites: Assumed: Bochner integration, Holder and Minkowski inequalities, completeness and the fundamental theorem for W^{1,1} Banach-valued trajectories.
Refreshable: relative compactness via finite nets and Simon's exact interval-integral criterion (stated in the text).
Bridge-required: nonlinear truncation, compact convex hull of a compact value set, two-point cone comparison and the endpoint calculations.

selections.reason: Explains nonnegative scaling and why neither subtraction closure nor the gauge triangle inequality is available.
Prevents the invalid gauge [u-v] on a nonadditive cone by retaining the two separate gauge terms.
Audits the weak derivative space and demonstrates the explicit estimate required to reach A0.
Complete cone principal: positive degree-one gauge, weak derivative and the exact excluded pair (infinity,1).
Provides the decisive failure calculation before the tools, fixing the inadmissible infinity endpoint.
Tests injectivity, measurable inverse lifts and norm matching before claiming a transfer; refuses blanket equivalence.
Separates compactness of K(u) from compactness of u with an explicit L1-distance computation.
Checks that the weak translation norm cannot be replaced by a target norm without the actual compactness/Ehrling bridge.
Complete image principal: bounds on u in L1 and on K(u) in Lr, with compactness only of the image.
Fixes strong Lp compactness on one finite interval, with separate linear, compact-image and cone inputs.
Supplies the exact imported interface: compact interior interval integrals plus target-exponent translations.
Complete linear principal: fixed X compactly in B, B in Y, and family-uniform translations in the weaker time norm.
Fixes the shortened interval (0,T-h) and the supremum over the whole family before the h-limit.
Explains why q=1 yields finite-p control but no small supremum modulus.
Identifies exactly where r>1 produces a small tail; loss of that estimate is not claimed to prove necessity.

required_steps: Obtain compact interval integrals from the X bound and invoke Simon in Y.
Choose the Ehrling parameter before the subsequence index to upgrade a Y-Cauchy subsequence.
Bound the exceptional-set measure and the L1 truncation error uniformly.
Prove compactness of the closed convex hull by finite nets and apply it to interval averages.
Transfer compactness to untruncated interval integrals and invoke Simon in the target exponent.
Derive a uniform supremum bound from W11 and the L1 time norm.
Use Fubini and bounded-amplitude interpolation for every finite p.
Use Holder for a supremum translation modulus only when q is greater than one.
Compute the ramp derivative bound and finite-p error.
Prove lack of L-infinity compactness from uniform-limit continuity or separated indices.
Calculate the pairwise L1 separation of dyadic sign functions and their constant squared images.
Normalize both cone points by the sum of their gauges and use compactness plus injectivity.
Derive the A1 supremum bound and control the gauge-truncation tail.
Obtain compact interval integrals and apply Simon using the correct derivative exponent.
Upgrade weak-space Cauchy convergence with the two-point Ehrling estimate.
Construct the degree-one inverse gauge and verify its compact embedding.
Compute the inverse-lift L1 bound and the W11 output bound.
Check matching derivative and output spaces and apply Maitre with the correct endpoint.
